rules.when: The patient asks for dutasteride and has not tried finasteride first.
rules.then: Dutasteride is not supplied; finasteride is offered first. In one case the refusal came by phone after payment, although the customer says the questionnaire had 'recommended dutasteride'.
rules.proof: Trustpilot reviews of 22 Jan 2021 (with a company reply of 2 Feb 2021 from the pharmacist manager: finasteride is first-line for patients who have not tried medication, after a September 2020 risk assessment) and 19 Aug 2025 (company reply: following clinical guidelines). https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/oxfordonlinepharmacy.co.uk?search=dutasteride

rules.when: The patient wants dutasteride while still taking finasteride.
rules.then: The prescription is declined; the patient is told to stop finasteride and reorder. Company reply: it is 'not a licensed regime'.
rules.proof: Trustpilot review of 19 Feb 2021 and company reply of 25 Feb 2021. Old; not confirmed as current. https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/oxfordonlinepharmacy.co.uk?search=dutasteride

rules.when: The patient asks for oral minoxidil above the usual dose (the limit itself is not stated).
rules.then: The higher dose is not supplied (part of the order was cancelled). Company reply: higher doses need a specialist prescriber.
rules.proof: Trustpilot review of 18 Nov 2025 and company reply of 21 Nov 2025. https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/oxfordonlinepharmacy.co.uk?search=minoxidil

rules.then: Extra checks may follow: the GP is told and asked to monitor; one order was cancelled until GP blood tests were done; the oedema risk is flagged in the consultation and the patient agrees to tell their doctor.
rules.proof: Trustpilot reviews of 2 May 2025, 4 Jun 2025 (with company reply of 16 Jun 2025) and 16 Jun 2025. https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/oxfordonlinepharmacy.co.uk?search=minoxidil

rules.when: A reorder is placed early, while the patient should still have supply left.
rules.then: The order is put on hold and queried, or declined by the doctor.
rules.proof: Trustpilot reviews of 30 Aug 2025 (order on hold, company asked why) and Dec 2025 / 16 Jan 2026 (doctor declined a repeat with three months' supply left). https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/oxfordonlinepharmacy.co.uk?search=hair

rules.when: A woman orders a hair-loss tablet (the tablet is not named).
rules.then: The order was refused in the one known case. Company reply: it must prescribe within its clinical team's limits, it is not a hair-loss specialist, and it is limited in what it can prescribe for female patients.
rules.proof: Trustpilot review of 17 Jun 2024 and company reply of 11 Jul 2024. https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/oxfordonlinepharmacy.co.uk?search=hair&page=3

rules.when: The patient takes antidepressants and orders finasteride.
rules.then: Finasteride was still prescribed in the one known case (the customer complained about this). So antidepressant use may not be a hard stop. One unverified account.
rules.proof: Trustpilot review of 23 Oct 2026 and company reply. https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/oxfordonlinepharmacy.co.uk?search=finasteride

rules.when: The prescriber judges the chosen treatment unsuitable after payment.
rules.then: The order is declined with a full refund (refunds can take about 5 working days), or an alternative is offered which the patient can accept or decline.

engineSummary: Oxford Online Pharmacy is a catalogue pharmacy, not a recommender. The customer picks a product and pack size, then completes a short (about 3-minute) questionnaire. The form screens sex, age, partner pregnancy, heart and blood-pressure problems, mood, liver and kidney disease, allergies and previous treatment, and asks consent to tell the GP. Hard limits sit mainly with the prescriber after payment: men only for finasteride, dutasteride and oral minoxidil; over 18; dutasteride only after 6+ months of finasteride; oral minoxidil 2.5 mg only, at the usual dose, with blood-pressure checks. Women go to a separate programme that needs a blood test. None of this was seen live; it comes from the company's pages and reviews.
strengths: Very wide range for men: generic and branded finasteride, dutasteride, oral minoxidil (generic and Loniten), a compounded finasteride + minoxidil + tretinoin spray, topical minoxidil and bundles.
Low, transparent pack prices with no subscription; long packs (168 tablets, 180 capsules) cut the monthly cost.
Clear safety stance: finasteride-first, off-label documents, GP informed, blood-pressure checks for oral minoxidil.
weaknesses: Payment is taken before the prescriber decides; refusals (dutasteride, early reorders, women) come after checkout.
Customer chooses the drug; the questionnaire does not appear to recommend or personalise a plan.
Weak women's offer: oral treatments refused, programme needs a blood test and the drug is not named; pages conflict.
Only 2.5 mg minoxidil tablets, so patients must split tablets for the usual starting dose.
opportunities: A guided consultation that recommends a plan (and screens before payment) would beat their pick-then-pay flow.
Women's hair loss: offer clear licensed and off-label options (topical minoxidil, oral minoxidil low dose, spironolactone) with transparent eligibility.
Lower-strength oral minoxidil (1.25 mg or less) to avoid tablet splitting.
Publish the compounded spray strengths and price clearly; Oxford does not.
Follow-up and progress tracking (photos, check-ins) are not part of their model.

limitations: The company's website could not be opened (Cloudflare check, HTTP 403) at stage 1 or stage 2. Product, price and consultation facts come from web-search snippets of the company's own pages, which are summaries of indexed copies of varying age, not the live pages.
The compounded spray (p8) is confirmed, but its strengths and price are not.
All findings come from Trustpilot reviews and company replies, paraphrased by a fetch tool that will not quote at length. Reviews are one-sided, unverified and some are years old.
The 'rules' are prescriber behaviour reported by customers, not engine behaviour seen in a replay. None has been tested.
Web search was unavailable (shared budget used up), so press, help-centre pages and regulator reports were not found.
Not every page of each Trustpilot search was read (for example 'finasteride' pages 2 to 4 and 'hair' page 5).
No one-change experiments were run: the consultation could not be reached. Every option-level effect is untested; rules are labelled docs or inferred.
No exact question wording or answer options are known, so flows[0].questions is empty; the topics list is a summary only.
Not tested: every one-change experiment in the protocol (sex, age, pregnancy, heart, blood pressure, liver, kidney, mood, medicines, allergies, previous treatment, preference).
